newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish government to lower 1997 CPI target to 12 pct.
newsitem.headline: Polish government to lower 1997 CPI target to 12 pct.

text.p: The Polish government will lower its official inflation target to year-on-year 12 percent in December this year from the currently planned 13 percent, Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Tuesday.
"According to information I have, we will adjust the inflation index for the end of the year to 12 percent. This will be our official target," Belka told a news conference after a government meeting.

He earlier said a downward adjustment of the inflation target was possible after low inflation in May, when consumer prices fell to 14.6 percent from April's 15.3 percent. Belka said on Monday he expected the CPI to further decline in June.

The government wants to curb inflation to below 10 percent next year. Consumer prices rose 6.6 percent in the January-May period, compared with a 10.3 percent rise in the corresponding period last year. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
